environment.description: Same container deployed on a hardened RHEL 9 host with a custom SELinux type enforcement policy (graphql_server_t). The TE policy confines the node process to type graphql_server_t with the following constraints: (1) allow graphql_server_t self:tcp_socket { create connect accept listen }; (2) allow graphql_server_t graphql_session_t:file { read write create getattr }; (3) The /tmp/sessions directory is labeled graphql_session_t. (4) Critically, the policy includes a dontaudit rule suppressing AVC denials for net_raw capability, and the process runs without CAP_NET_RAW. The SELinux boolean httpd_can_network_connect is set to off. The node process type graphql_server_t has NO allow rule for network connect to external ports (only accept/listen on its bound port 4000). Outbound connections from the process are denied by SELinux with type=AVC denied { name_connect }. Additionally, the host runs with iptables OUTPUT chain DROP policy for the container's UID except established connections to the ALB health check endpoint.

config.runtime: RHEL 9, SELinux enforcing, custom TE policy graphql_server_t
te_policy_key_rules: allow graphql_server_t graphql_port_t:tcp_socket { accept listen bind };
allow graphql_server_t graphql_session_t:file { read write create getattr };
# NO name_connect rule - outbound TCP blocked
config.iptables: OUTPUT chain policy DROP for uid=1001 (node), ACCEPT only for ESTABLISHED,RELATED
config.network_note: Padding oracle requires many sequential requests; the oracle itself still responds, but the attacker cannot exfiltrate decrypted data via outbound connections from the server. The oracle distinguishes padding errors in response messages.
